title: Cohomological dimension of a smooth curve
statement:
For a smooth separated connected curve $C$
over an algebraically closed field and any torsion
etale sheaf $F$,
one has $H^q(C,F)=0$ for $q>2$, with cohomology as in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: *Setup.* Let $C$ be the smooth separated connected curve over the algebraically closed field $k$ and $F$ the torsion sheaf. By [lem-sc-affine-open-finite-complement] there is an affine open $U\subseteq C$, with inclusion $j:U\to C$, whose complement $S=C\setminus U$ is a finite set of closed points. For $x\in S$ the residue field $\kappa(x)$ equals $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] ($C$ is of finite type over $k$), hence is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]; so $U\subseteq C$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sc-finite-support-acyclic] and [lem-sc-iso-off-finite-set-cohomology]. By [lem-sc-etale-affine-over-curve] (with $w=\mathrm{id}_U$) $U$ is an affine curve over $k$. The morphism $j$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]: for an affine open $W\subseteq C$ the preimage $j^{-1}(W)=U\cap W$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], $C$ being separated over $k$.

proof.text: *Reduction to $j_*$, for $F$ killed by $n$.* Let $n\ge1$ and let $F$ (in this step and steps 3-8) be an abelian sheaf on $C_{\Et}$ with $n\cdot\mathrm{id}_F=0$; put $G=j^{-1}F$, also killed by $n$ since $j^{-1}$ is additive [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $\eta_F:F\to j_*j^{-1}F=j_*G$ be the unit of $j^{-1}\dashv j_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. By the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{j^{-1}F}\circ j^{-1}(\eta_F)=\mathrm{id}$, and $\varepsilon_{j^{-1}F}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sc-open-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful]; so $j^{-1}(\eta_F)$ is an isomorphism, and [lem-sc-iso-off-finite-set-cohomology] gives $H^q(C,F)\cong H^q(C,j_*G)$ for all $q\ge2$. It therefore suffices for $q=3$ to show $H^3(C,j_*G)=0$ (steps 3-7).

proof.text: *Two acyclic envelopes on $U$.* By [lem-sc-torsion-acyclic-envelope] on $U$ there is a short exact sequence $0\to G\to J\to G'\to0$ in $\Ab(U_{\Et})$ with $J$ killed by $n$, $H^q(U,J)=0$, $H^q(C,j_*J)=0$ and $H^q(W,w^{-1}J)=0$ for all $q\ge1$ and every etale $w:W\to U$; the cokernel $G'$ is killed by $n$ (a quotient of $J$). Applying the same lemma to $G'$ gives $0\to G'\to J'\to G''\to0$ with the same properties for $J'$ and $G''$ killed by $n$. A sheaf killed by $n$ is torsion in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] (every section is killed by $n$).

source.place: split along the Lean proof WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/HighDegreeVanishing.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_of_three_le_of_forall (lines 274-437): lines 314-327 (exists_mono_acyclic_of_nsmul_eq_zero twice, S1, S2)

proof.text: *$H^1(C,j_*G'')=0$.* The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] of $0\to G'\to J'\to G''\to0$ on $U$ contains $H^1(U,J')\to H^1(U,G'')\to H^2(U,G')$; here $H^1(U,J')=0$ (step 3) and $H^2(U,G')=0$ by [lem-sc-affine-curve-h2-vanishing] ($U$ is an affine curve by step 1, $G'$ is torsion), so $H^1(U,G'')=0$. The edge map $H^1(C,j_*G'')\to H^1(U,G'')$ is injective by [lem-sc-edge-map-h1-injective], hence $H^1(C,j_*G'')=0$.

source.place: split along the Lean proof WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/HighDegreeVanishing.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_of_three_le_of_forall (lines 274-437): lines 328-338 (hc, hd)

proof.text: *$0\to j_*G'\to j_*J'\to j_*G''\to0$ is exact.* Exactness on the left and in the middle is left exactness of $j_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For surjectivity let $V\to C$ be etale and $s\in(j_*G'')(V)=G''(V\times_CU)$. Cover $V$ by affine opens $V_a$; these form a covering of $V$ in $C_{\Et}$. Put $W_a=V_a\times_CU$. It is affine, being affine over the affine $V_a$ as a base change of the affine morphism $j$ (step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1), (2)), and etale over $U$ as a base change of $V_a\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; so $W_a$ is an affine curve over $k$ by [lem-sc-etale-affine-over-curve]. Restricting $0\to G\to J\to G'\to0$ along $w_a:W_a\to U$ gives a short exact sequence, inverse image being exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (with $R=\mathbf Z$); its long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] contains $H^1(W_a,w_a^{-1}J)\to H^1(W_a,w_a^{-1}G')\to H^2(W_a,w_a^{-1}G)$, where the left group is $0$ by step 3 and the right one by [lem-sc-affine-curve-h2-vanishing] ($w_a^{-1}G$ is killed by $n$, hence torsion). So $H^1(W_a,w_a^{-1}G')=0$, and [lem-sc-lift-sections-h1-vanishing] applied to $0\to G'\to J'\to G''\to0$ and $W_a\in U_{\Et}$ lifts $s|_{V_a}\in G''(W_a)$ to $J'(W_a)=(j_*J')(V_a)$. Thus $j_*J'\to j_*G''$ is locally surjective, hence an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective].

proof.text: *$H^2(C,j_*G')=0$.* The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] of the short exact sequence of step 5 contains $H^1(C,j_*G'')\to H^2(C,j_*G')\to H^2(C,j_*J')$; the left group is $0$ by step 4 and the right one by step 3 ([lem-sc-torsion-acyclic-envelope] (2) for $J'$).

source.place: split along the Lean proof WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/HighDegreeVanishing.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_of_three_le_of_forall (lines 274-437): lines 368-377 (hh)

proof.text: *$H^3(C,j_*G)=0$, hence $H^3(C,F)=0$.* By left exactness of $j_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $0\to j_*G\to j_*J\to j_*G'$ is exact. Let $N=\operatorname{coker}(j_*G\to j_*J)$, so that $0\to j_*G\to j_*J\to N\to0$ is exact and $j_*J\to j_*G'$ induces a monomorphism $\psi:N\to j_*G'$; let $R=\operatorname{coker}\psi$. The functor $j^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and through the counit isomorphisms $j^{-1}j_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ of [lem-sc-open-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful] (natural in the sheaf) $j^{-1}$ of $j_*J\to j_*G'$ is $J\to G'$, an epimorphism; so $j^{-1}\psi$ is an epimorphism and $j^{-1}R=0$. By [lem-sc-finite-support-acyclic] (step 1) $H^q(C,R)=0$ for $q\ge1$. The long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] of $0\to N\to j_*G'\to R\to0$ and of $0\to j_*G\to j_*J\to N\to0$ give $0=H^1(C,R)\to H^2(C,N)\to H^2(C,j_*G')=0$ (step 6), so $H^2(C,N)=0$, and $H^2(C,N)\to H^3(C,j_*G)\to H^3(C,j_*J)=0$ (step 3, [lem-sc-torsion-acyclic-envelope] (2)), so $H^3(C,j_*G)=0$. By step 2, $H^3(C,F)=0$.

proof.text: *All $q\ge3$ for sheaves killed by $n$ (dimension shifting on $C$).* Induction on $q\ge3$, simultaneously for all sheaves killed by $n$; the case $q=3$ is step 7. For $q>3$ and $F$ killed by $n$, [lem-sc-torsion-acyclic-envelope] on $C$ gives $0\to F\to J_C\to F_1\to0$ with $J_C$ killed by $n$ and $H^{q}(C,J_C)=0$; $F_1$ is killed by $n$. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] contains $H^{q-1}(C,F_1)\to H^q(C,F)\to H^q(C,J_C)=0$, and $H^{q-1}(C,F_1)=0$ by induction ($q-1\ge3$). So $H^q(C,F)=0$.

proof.text: *Torsion sheaves.* Let now $F$ be any torsion sheaf. By [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union] $F=\varinjlim_mF[m]$, a filtered colimit of the subsheaves $F[m]=\ker(m:F\to F)$, each killed by $m$. The curve $C$ is quasi-compact (of finite type over $k$) and quasi-separated (separated), so by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] $H^q(C,F)=\varinjlim_mH^q(C,F[m])$, which is $0$ for $q\ge3$ by step 8. Hence $H^q(C,F)=0$ for all $q>2$.
